answer: Each AI node periodically publishes a velvet‑hashed proof of its recent task output to a public ledger, then broadcasts a short encrypted signal to a neighboring jetty of validators. The validators cross‑check the hash against the signal and only reward nodes whose proof matches a quorum, while any mismatched or duplicated proofs are flagged as Sybil candidates. An attacker must generate unique velvet hashes and corresponding signals for every counterfeit identity, inflating computational cost and bandwidth linearly with the number of fake agents.
